status: post-opening response-trait hypothesis frozen before temporal validation readback
ecological_question: Do frog species have temporally repeatable activation geometry—i.e., when they gain acoustic incidences under wetter conditions, do they consistently favor newly active sites versus sites that were already active?

gain_event.wet_gain_incidence: species detected at a stop in the wetter run but not at that same stop in the drier run
gain_event.success: wet-gain incidence occurs at a stop with zero calling species in the drier run
gain_event.failure: wet-gain incidence occurs at a stop that already contains >=1 calling species in the drier run

opportunity_correction.q_pair: fraction of the ten drier-run stops that are acoustically inactive
opportunity_correction.informative_pair_rule: use only 0 < q_pair < 1; q_pair=0 or 1 contains no spatial-choice information and is excluded structurally before fitting
opportunity_correction.interpretation: species intercept >0 means wet gains occur at newly active sites more often than expected from their availability; intercept <0 means gains are concentrated in already-active sites

species_trait_labels.zero: gain placement proportional to available inactive versus active stops

overlap_family.rule: intersection of species with finite activation_geometry_log_odds and SE in both periods

primary_test.metric: Spearman rank correlation between early and late activation_geometry_log_odds

prespecified_sensitivities.weighted_regression: WLS late_geometry ~ early_geometry weighted by inverse late-period variance with HC3 covariance; expected positive slope
prespecified_sensitivities.sign_concordance: fraction of species retaining edge-activator versus local-deepener sign; one-sided exact binomial test against 0.5
prespecified_sensitivities.family_adjusted: WLS late_geometry ~ early_geometry + C(Family) when coverage and residual df permit

secondary_descriptives: species-level early and late geometry estimates with 95% CIs
fraction of wet-gain incidences at newly active sites by species before opportunity correction
correlation of activation geometry with conventional four-axis functional traits; descriptive only and not used to redefine the trait
interpretation_if_supported: Species possess a repeatable response trait describing how rainfall-associated acoustic gains enter the spatial community matrix, even if conventional life-history traits do not predict rainfall-response magnitude.
interpretation_if_null: Do not promote activation geometry as a stable species trait; retain the community-level four-quadrant decomposition only.
boundaries: This is a response trait of observed acoustic activation geometry, not occupancy niche, dispersal ability, colonization strategy or demographic life history.
The same species occur in both temporal periods; this is temporal validation, not independent-species replication.
No rainfall causality or physiological mechanism claim.
No alternative time split, eligibility threshold, opportunity correction or spatial-edge definition may replace the frozen specification after readback.
